chapter_title: Concerning the worn and torn apart Garments, or th
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶2:** What then are these "great external truths"? Or again, what you sometimes call the "degraded truths" — what are those degraded truths? Or the "devastated and fragmented truths"? Or what are the "semblances and remnants of truth in their ruined state"? Or what is this name, "the essential substance of wisdom"? Or conversely, what is the "suffering of wisdom bound in temptation"? Or why is it named otherwise, "the Divine calling toward life"? Or what is "the interior life that is destroyed" — annihilated, subjugated, and consumed within the power of evil? What are all these spiritual states?

---

**¶3:** How has the one wisdom been differentiated into all these designations and taken on these altered conditions of existence?

---

**¶7:** The external truths named "great" are the five faculties of the understanding that complete the form of the ascending structure of Divine Truth — the fully regenerated Divine Human. These were purified by the descent of the Divine into manifestation.

---

**¶8:** In contrast, those named "degraded truths": the degraded truths are the devoured illuminating wisdom. It is compounded and entangled in the general form of the created order, within the ruling falsities that dominate from the interior, which persist throughout all the doctrinal structures that separate one degree from another. And its radiance is that which shines forth and is displayed in the knowledges that are bound in their fixed series and in the faculties that govern the natural progression. And likewise, these degraded truths that are entangled in the three natural degrees below — above the sustaining principle at the lowest foundation [GAP-1] — upon the natural plane that lies beneath the sustaining principle. These are named "degraded truths" because [GAP-2] established [GAP-3]

---

**¶9:** However, the "great devastated and fragmented truths" which we have set forth — this is the entangled living influx of the Divine. It is harvested, severed, and consumed. It is overpowered by the five corporeal domains of the proprium, which insinuate themselves as they advance from state to state.

---

**¶10:** On the other hand, [GAP-4: REVIEW these] we have termed the "semblances and great remnants of truth in their ruined state" [GAP-5] are the three encompassing external truths of understanding, of love, and of truth itself. These the Lord's operative Divine Truth clothed upon His external form. With them He set all things in the spiritual world into order. With them also He emptied the containing forms of their falsities. He swept them clean and laid them bare before the sustaining principle at the foundation of all things.

---

**¶11:** Conversely, "the essential substances of wisdom" — we have called them by this name — are the living power that remains within all things in the natural degree. It rises through the receptive states within all natural conditions, gathering itself together and pouring forth upon all things.

---

**¶12:** And then, the "[GAP-6: REVIEW Light] suffering of wisdom in temptation" — [GAP-7: REVIEW we have termed] this bound "illuminating power of the Divine." It [GAP-8] all [GAP-9] upon the natural plane, in what is without good and in what is conjoined with good.

---

**¶13:** Also, that which is named "the Divine calling toward life" is the summons from the Divine and the obedient response of the human will. It moves within all the faculties and powers we have named. It awakens them, brings them peace, and impels them toward their proper function and activity.

---

**¶14:** That which is named "the interior life that is destroyed" — which is annihilated, subjugated, and consumed — this is the living power within the goods of works, the natural goods of use, and the interior truths still in their seminal state. These shall be threshed out, plucked away, and cut down, and they give sustenance to the corporeal domains of the proprium. Furthermore: the perception that has lost all its living good, and the external truth that has become wholly devastated — these shall perish. Again, this is a portion of the entire interior life that is destroyed and annihilated; since even this whole portion of it they destroy [GAP-10]

---

**¶15:** For all these designations [GAP-11] are a single [GAP-12] since the beginning, it [GAP-13] as it illuminates all things; but they were separated into all these distinct conditions in the first great temptation-combat. They became established in all these altered forms and received these many names. Of course, if now all these varieties are laid bare and stripped of all these outward appearances and parted from all these designations, they will gather together and constitute a single form and a single name — unaltered and unchangeable forever — in the realm of their first Divine essence, from which they were sent forth against the power of evil.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: what then are these 'great garments'? Or again, this you sometimes call the 'rags', what are those 'rags'? Or the 'worn and torn apart'? Or what are the 'images and the tattered clothes'? Or what is this name: 'light element'? Or conversely, what is the 'Cross of Light'? Or why named otherwise: the 'counsel of life'? Or what is the 'soul that is slain'; being killed, oppressed, and murdered in the enemy? What are all these names?
how have they changed with all these names and become set in altered forms
The garments that are named 'great garment' are the five intellectuals that make perfect the body of the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. They were purified by the coming of the Ambassador.

In contrast, the ones named 'rag': the rags are the devoured enlightening power. It is compounded and entangled in the body of the universe in the rulers who are above, who exist in all the firmaments. Also, its shine is that which lights up and is displayed in the stars of the chain and the powers of the course. And likewise, these rags that are entangled in these three earths below, above the head of the Porter [and also] on the earth that is under the Porter. These are named the 'rags', because [they are] set [apart in every place]

However, the 'great worn and torn apart garments', which we have proclaimed, is this entangled living power. It is reaped, cut, and devoured. It is overpowered by the five worlds of the flesh, which creep as they move from place to place.

On the other hand, [these] we have termed the 'images and the great tattered clothes' [they] are the three great garments of the wind, the fire, and the water. These the Living Spirit cloaked upon his body. With them he set in order things in the universe. With them also he emptied the vessels. He swept them out and laid them bare in front of the Porter at the foundation of all things.

Conversely, '[the ele]ments', we have called them this name, are this power that remains in all things below. It rises up in the wombs of all the earths, gathering together, and pouring forth upon all things.
And then, the '[Light] Cross' [we have termed] this bound 'light power'. It [is spread in] all [things] upon the earth, in the dry and the moist.
Also, the one named the 'counsel of life' is the summons and the obedience. It moves in all these powers that we have named. It awakens them, gives them ease, and drives them to their movement.

The one named 'the soul that is slain', which is killed, oppressed and murdered; it is this power of fruit, vegetables and seeds. They shall be threshed, plucked and cut down; and they give nourishment to the worlds of the flesh. Further: the wood should it be dry, and the garment should it become ragged, will perish. Again, it is [a pa]rt of this entire soul that is slain and killed; since also even this whole part of it they kill [and devour]

For all these names [that we have proclaimed] are a single [power] since the beginning, it [was one] as it enlightens; but they separated into all these parts in this first contest. They became set in all these altered forms, and these many names. Of course, if now all these varieties are laid bare, and stripped of all these appearances, and parted from all these names; they will gather together and make a single form, and a single name, unaltered and unchangeable for ever in the land of their first essence, from which they were sent forth against the enemy.

fills.explanation: The text enumerates two locations of the rags (above the Porter's head and on the earth beneath him), requiring a simple conjunction to bridge the two spatial references within the three earths below.

The explanatory pattern throughout the chapter uses a subject-copula construction before the defining predicate; "they are set" forms the passive construction explaining why these powers are called rags.

The metaphor of 'rags' (torn cloth) corresponds to the light being set apart/scattered throughout the cosmos; the degraded truths are established in fragmented distribution across all locations, explaining why they bear the name 'rags.'

The editor's 'these' fits the chapter's consistent pattern of using a demonstrative pronoun to introduce each named category before its identification (cf. ¶8 'the ones named,' ¶11 'we have called them').

A resumptive pronoun is needed to serve as the subject of 'are the three great garments'; the Kephalaia commonly uses resumptive pronouns after an extended naming clause before the copula identification.

The editor's 'Light' is confirmed: the standard Manichaean term 'Cross of Light' is established in ¶2 of this same chapter, and the spiritual reading consistently identifies this as the suffering of illuminating wisdom bound in the natural plane.

The editor's 'we have termed' is confirmed: it matches the chapter's consistent attribution pattern (cf. ¶10 'we have termed,' ¶11 'we have called them this name') and correctly introduces the identification of the Cross of Light with the bound light power.

The Cross of Light is the Divine wisdom extended/spread across all of nature; 'spread' captures the cross imagery of being stretched across the natural plane and matches the Manichaean concept of light dispersed throughout material creation.

Completing the standard Kephalaia phrase 'all things upon the earth'; the spiritual reading confirms this refers to all that exists upon the natural plane, in states without good (dry) and conjoined with good (moist).

The chapter consistently pairs 'kill' with 'devour' when describing the destruction of the soul in matter (cf. ¶9 'devoured,' ¶14 'give nourishment to the worlds of the flesh'); the consumption/devouring of the light by the proprium completes the destruction sequence.

The chapter uses attribution phrases throughout (¶9 'which we have proclaimed,' ¶10 'we have termed,' ¶11 'we have called'); 'that we have proclaimed' echoes ¶9's exact phrasing and suits the summary function of ¶15.

The chapter consistently uses 'power' as its fundamental term for the one light substance in its various states (enlightening power, living power, light power); all these names designate one single power that was undifferentiated before the first contest.

The passage contrasts the original unified state ('was one as it enlightens') with the subsequent fragmentation ('but they separated into all these parts'), and ¶15's conclusion that all varieties will 'gather together and make a single form' confirms the original state was unity.
